plan: Store the constructor's data dict as a deep copy; it is the single mutable source of truth, and to_data() returns a deep copy of it.
Represent the part-whole structure directly as the nested dicts/lists: workspace and container items (section, group) hold 'items' lists; notes and references are leaves.

Implement total_word_count with one recursive walker that dispatches on kind: notes count \b\w+\b words after stripping [[?id]] marker tokens (replaced by a space so markers never merge adjacent words), references contribute their declared word_count, containers recurse.

Implement unresolved_markers with a recursive walker collecting marker identifiers from note text (regex on the exact [[?identifier]] form) and reference 'unresolved' lists into a set, returned sorted lexicographically.
Implement outline as a deterministic depth-first traversal in list order: workspace title first, then '  ' * level + '<kind>: <title>' per item, children indented one level deeper.

Implement move with strict validate-then-mutate ordering: check both ids are strings, locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), reject non-containers, reject moving a container into itself or any of its descendants (containment/no-cycle check), and range-check an explicit index against 0..len(destination). Only after every check passes, pop the item and append/insert it, so any raised ValueError leaves the tree untouched.
Locate items with a single recursive finder returning (parent_list, position, item), reused for both the moved item and the destination.
mechanisms: Composite tree: uniform 'item' records where sections/groups contain child item lists and notes/references are leaves
Kind-dispatched recursive aggregation for total_word_count (marker-stripped regex word count for notes, declared word_count for references)
Recursive set-union collection of unresolved marker identifiers, returned as a sorted unique list
Deterministic depth-first outline rendering with two-space-per-level indentation
Containment invariant: only workspace/section/group accept children, and a container may not be moved into itself or a descendant
Atomic move via full validation before any mutation (failed moves provably leave to_data() unchanged)
Defensive deep copies on construction and in to_data()
